results.question: Which visible guidance phase is shown here? Describe the visible evidence and any limits on declaring the phase complete.
results.reference_answer: Further tooling operations are shown, with a spindle or tool positioned over mounted metal blocks. The film does not establish one continuous tracked part.

observation.summary: The latest view shows a vertical machine head with a slender, ball-ended probe above a circular opening, surrounded by copper-coloured blocks held on round metal fixtures. Small curled fragments are visible along block edges; the separately displayed products appeared only in earlier shots.
observation.guidance: Record the tool-over-mounted-tooling view under S4, keeping probe contact and measurement results unconfirmed. Distinguish visible positioning from verified inspection to reduce the risk of treating promotional footage as quality evidence.
observation.principle: A visible tool position supports an observation checkpoint, not instrument accuracy, part acceptance, or continuity of production across edited shots.
observation.concern: No clear operational hazard is established; the probe's exact contact with the opening is not distinguishable in this view.

results.question: Which visible guidance phase is shown here? Describe the visible evidence and any limits on declaring the phase complete.
results.reference_answer: A brief circular monochrome imaging view interrupts the operative sequence. This is a change of displayed view, not a diagnostic conclusion.

observation.summary: The latest image shows a circular monochrome imaging field on a black background, with dark branching lines and a thin diagonal linear object entering from the lower left. This replaces the historically visible colored endoscopic field; operative tissue and working tips are no longer currently visible.
observation.guidance: Record the switch to circular imaging as the current visual phase, and watch for an actual return to the colored endoscopic field. Treat the cut as a break in evidence rather than proof of continuous instrument handling or a clinical result.
observation.principle: Recognizing an imaging-view change reduces the risk of conflating edited scenes; it does not establish a diagnostic interpretation or procedural success.
observation.concern: No specific visible potential issue is established; the monochrome view does not support assessment of the previously shown operative contacts.

results.question: Which visible guidance phase is shown here? Describe the visible evidence and any limits on declaring the phase complete.
results.reference_answer: The straight-bar starting position is shown. Both hands hold a straight-shaft bar low before the curl demonstration, without verified plate load or equipment checks.

observation.summary: The demonstrator stands with arms lowered; a straight metal bar and its right black weight are visible at the bottom of the latest image, with the left hand and opposite end cropped. Recent frames within one second show both hands holding the shaft low in front of the thighs.
observation.guidance: Record the visible straight-bar starting position, but do not count a curl yet. Assess a raise and return only when both positions can be followed in the same uninterrupted shot.
observation.principle: Separating visible starting states from complete movement cycles reduces unsupported repetition and technique judgments; it does not establish equipment security or exercise safety.
observation.concern: The bottom crop limits current inspection of the left grip and opposite bar end; no specific equipment problem is established.
